title: Cross-Functional Career Activation Playbook
author: Diego Morales
content:
Executive summary

Purpose: This playbook provides a unified, repeatable approach to activating new hires and internal movers across role ladders, benefits enrollment, and internal tooling so that employees reach contribution velocity faster and hiring managers have a clear, auditable workflow. It covers the first 120 days, cross-functional rotation mechanics, benefit milestones, and the minimal set of artifacts teams must produce.

Who should use this document
- People-ops partners and hiring managers
- Team leads and rotation hosts
- New joiners and internal applicants for mobility

Top-level commitments
- People-ops responds to access escalations within 8 business hours.
- Time-to-first-merge target for technical hires: <= 21 days.
- Benefits enrollment completion target by Day 14: 95%+

1) Onboarding timeline and responsibilities (Day 0 to Day 120)
- Day 0 (offer accepted): People-ops creates a record, schedules orientation, and triggers SSO provisioning. Owner: People-ops.
- Day 1: Kickoff orientation (company values, security baseline, benefits overview). Manager assigns buddy and first-week goals. Owner: Manager + People-ops.
- Day 2	6: Access and micro-onboarding: grant GitHub, Jira, CI dashboards; complete role-specific security CBT. Owner: Eng Dev Tools + Manager.
- Day 70: First PR and systems ownership shadowing; benefits enrollment should be completed. Owner: Employee + People-ops.
- Day 3120: Transition to owner of a small feature or operational task; career ladder checkpoint at Day 90. Owner: Manager.

2) Role ladder alignment and signals
- Reference the canonical career rubric (link in related_pages). At the Day 90 checkpoint, managers document signals observed using the Mobility Signal Sheet (one-line per signal): impact, ownership, cross-team collaboration, quality.
- Signals that trigger an internal mobility conversation: repeated cross-team recommendations, delivery of a cross-functional project, or explicit employee interest with documented learning steps.

3) Cross-functional rotations (structure and guardrails)
- Rotation purpose: targeted exposure, not role transfer. Typical length: 4	6 weeks for short exploratory rotations, 12 weeks for deeper skill transfer.
- Eligibility: at least 6 weeks in current role for new joiners; internal applicants need manager approval.
- Deliverables required for a rotation to be considered complete: one merged contribution (code, doc, or process change), a recorded 305 minute knowledge share, and a completed handoff checklist.
- Ownership: home manager retains performance review responsibility; host manager provides day-to-day mentorship and a written recommendation at rotation close.

4) Benefits activation checklist (concise)
- Invite to benefits portal sent on offer acceptance.
- Live enrollment Q&A within the first week.
- Confirmation of payroll elections on first paycheck.
- People-ops will send a benefits activation confirmation email when coverages are active.

Common benefit issues and remedies
- Missing portal access: verify Okta status, then escalate to it-support@redwood.com.
- Enrollment not reflected in payroll: send a ticket to benefits@redwood.com with the employee ID and screenshots.
- Dependent coverage disputes: benefits team requests supporting documents and processes changes through Workday.

5) Internal tooling access matrix (owners and minimal request steps)
- Okta / SSO: Owner - IT/Security. Action: auto-provision; if missing, open an IT ticket.
- GitHub org: Owner - Eng Dev Tools. Action: manager adds to team repo; submit infra-access form for elevated roles.
- Jira & product boards: Owner - Product Ops. Action: manager assigns project role.
- Workday / People-ops portal: Owner - People-ops. Action: people-ops sends invite and enrollment packets.
- Cost & performance dashboards: Owner - Platform Analytics. Action: analytics form to request read access.

6) Minimal artifacts every team must provide for host rotations and new hires
- 2-week micro-onboarding plan that lists concrete tasks for Day 14.
- Mentor/buddy assignment with contact info.
- Published team README with architecture overview and runbook links.
- PR triage guidelines and coding standards link.

7) Manager playbook snippets (copy-and-paste friendly)
- Approval email for rotations: "I approve [EMPLOYEE] for a [DURATION] rotation on [HOST_TEAM]. Goals: [GOALS]. Home 1:1s continue weekly. Host manager: please publish a 2-week micro-onboarding plan before start."
- Access escalation subject line: "Onboarding access escalation: [EMPLOYEE NAME] - missing [RESOURCE]"

8) Measurement and feedback loop
- Quarterly metrics published by People-ops: time-to-first-access, time-to-first-merge, benefits enrollment rate, rotation satisfaction (survey mean).
- Post-rotation survey questions (examples): usefulness of mentorship, clarity of deliverables, and likelihood to recommend rotation.
- People-ops will run an annual calibration workshop with managers to review mobility outcomes.

9) Regional considerations
- EU: statutory waiting periods and enrollment rules may alter the Day 30 activation expectation; people-ops EU will annotate offer letters with local timelines.
- APAC: local vendors handle some benefits; cross-time-zone rotations should define 2 hour synchronous overlap minimum unless agreed otherwise.

10) Troubleshooting common scenarios
- If an employee cannot complete a rotation due to urgent home priorities, document the reason and pause with a renegotiated end-date.
- If an employee reports harassment or psychological safety concerns during rotation, notify people-ops and security immediately; follow the incident response and HR investigation workflow.

Appendix: templates and links
- Rotation agreement template: short paragraph stored in the People-ops portal.
- Micro-onboarding template: accessible in internal templates library.
- Career ladder rubric: see related_pages link.
- People-ops portal: https://people.redwood.internal/onboarding

Document owner and cadence
- Owner: People-ops (Diego Morales).
- Review cadence: annual review each November; interim updates as legal or tool changes occur.
